meetingTitle: Raffles Place Flagship & App Promo Launch

card.youAre: You are Wei Ling, Operations Director looking after the shop floor, Auntie Mary, food hygiene, and the budget.
facts: Our 28-seat Raffles Place shop has four 4-seater booths (16 seats) with 12 wall sockets and free guest Wi-Fi, plus six 2-seater tables.
Four freelancers held the 4-seater booths for two hours every morning this week on a single $2.20 drink, costing about $420 a morning in lost breakfast sets.

Auntie Mary (62) is the only floor staff who seats solo diners with hot trays and clears tables. A customer in a suit shouted at her last week when she moved his tissue packet, and she will not police seats or touch customers' belongings.
60% of our morning customers dine solo and cannot carry a hot tray of runny soft-boiled eggs without a table.
A customer from our soft trial was hospitalized yesterday with suspected salmonella from soft-boiled eggs; SFA inspectors arrive tomorrow morning at 9:00 AM.
Our egg sous-vide bath dipped below 60°C for 45 minutes during yesterday's rush; pulling soft-boiled eggs completely wipes out 60% of breakfast set orders ($1,800/morning).

Delivery platforms take a 32% commission on breakfast sets ($3.20 on a $10 set), turning delivery orders net-negative. Using our floor staff for in-house deliveries carries rain surge and traffic accident liability.
Our storeroom has two unopened cartons of pasteurized backup eggs ready to heat to 63°C (22 minutes per batch).
card.responsibility: Make sure our plans work for Auntie Mary and the counter staff without breaking food hygiene or blowing our margin.

card.youAre: You are Arjun, Tech & POS Lead looking after the self-order kiosks, the kitchen docket printer, and store power.
facts: The 15-inch kiosk screen fits 12 drink buttons per page and about 18 characters per line.

The kitchen docket currently prints the same button name the customer sees, so renaming a button changes what the kitchen reads. POS v2.4 can hold a separate kitchen print name, but it has to be configured and tested before the morning rush.
When English names printed on kitchen dockets at Tampines, our 65-year-old kopi uncles slowed down by 15 seconds a cup.
The 12 booth wall sockets and guest Wi-Fi run on a programmable smart relay breaker in the back room. Cutting power also hits paying customers using the sockets.

Raising our GrabFood menu price by 30% ($13 for a toast set) triggers platform price-parity penalties, while our direct web QR link only supports self-pickup because the POS has no rider dispatch integration.
POS changes made tonight still need a short kitchen test before 8am.
card.responsibility: Keep the kiosks, kitchen printer, and store power simple enough to configure and test tonight.

card.youAre: You are Mei, Menu & Store Experience Lead looking after our kopi and kaya toast recipes, the menu, and customer flow.
facts: In yesterday's Raffles Place trial, 19 of 28 first-time kiosk users froze for over 2 minutes at 'Kopi O Kosong', 'Kopi C Siew Dai' or 'Teh Halia', and 72% missed the small corner language toggle.

Soft-boiled eggs require continuous 63°C holding to prevent salmonella enteritidis; heating a fresh pasteurized backup batch takes 22 minutes and cannot be rushed without ruining the runny yolk texture.
60% of our morning crowd dines solo while carrying hot trays of runny soft-boiled eggs.
Corporate CBD towers order 20+ toast sets at once on shared GrabFood group carts; if we de-list from GrabFood, office admins will immediately switch orders to Ya Kun.
Local regulars mocked a rival kopitiam on Reddit when it renamed Kopi O to 'Local Americano'.
card.responsibility: Keep our kopi and kaya toast authentic while making ordering and finding a seat easier.

card.youAre: You are Daniel, Marketing Lead looking after TikTok reviews, store promos, and public goodwill.
facts: A soft-trial diner was hospitalized yesterday with suspected salmonella (hospital lab results take 48 hours); Straits Times journalists arrive at 8:00 AM for our ribbon-cutting, and SFA inspectors arrive at 9:00 AM.
GrabFood and Foodpanda deliver 50% of our peak morning volume; de-listing wipes out $2,400 in morning sales and hands the CBD corporate market to competitors.
Adding a 30% price markup on GrabFood ($13 for a $10 toast set) breaches platform price-parity visibility rules and risks immediate customer backlash.
Google reviews dropped to 3.6 stars during our soft trial because breakfast walk-ins could not find a seat while laptop campers held the 4-seater booths for two hours.
card.responsibility: Protect our launch reputation and corporate CBD accounts without making promises the kitchen or floor staff cannot keep.

card.youAre: You are Sam, General Manager chairing the huddle.
facts: Call on the lead for each topic and let the team hash out the practical catches.
Make sure each topic wraps up with a clear call and someone owning the follow-up.
card.responsibility: Chair the huddle, hear both sides out, and assign a follow-up owner for each topic.

agenda.title: First-timers stalling at the kiosk over Kopi names
agenda.decision: how do we help first-time customers order Kopi confidently without slowing the kitchen or losing our kopitiam identity?

openingViews.view: In yesterday's trial at Raffles Place, 19 out of 28 first-time customers froze at our self-order kiosk because they didn't know what 'Kopi O Kosong' or 'Siew Dai' meant, and the queue backed out into the mall walkway. We open tomorrow at 8am, so we need to make ordering clear for newcomers without losing our kopitiam roots.

The catch is that whatever name we put on the kiosk button also prints straight onto the kitchen ticket, and our 65-year-old kopi uncles rely on short local names to brew fast during the morning rush. Plus, the 15-inch screen only fits 12 buttons on one page.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Kiosk ordering freeze: 19 of 28 first-timers stalled at 'Kopi O Kosong' and 72% missed the corner language toggle, backing queues out into the mall walkway.
tradeOffs.question: How do we make the drink choices clear for a first-timer standing at the kiosk?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Kitchen ticket & screen space: The kitchen printer prints the button name, and the 15-inch screen only fits 12 buttons per page (18 characters per line).
tradeOffs.question: How do we keep the kitchen ticket fast for our kopi uncles without pushing half the drinks onto page two?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Morning rush speed: When long English drink names printed on kitchen tickets at Tampines, our kopi uncles slowed down by 15 seconds a cup.
tradeOffs.question: How do we make sure our kopi uncles aren't slowed down reading new tickets during the 8am rush?

agenda.title: Morning seat crunch & laptop campers
agenda.decision: how do we free up tables for breakfast diners without turning Auntie Mary into seat police or punishing solo customers?

openingViews.view: Our Google rating dropped to 3.6 stars during the trial because breakfast customers couldn't find a seat. Freelancers plug into our wall sockets and camp at our four 4-seater booths for two hours over a single $2.20 coffee—locking up 16 of our 28 seats—and Auntie Mary got yelled at yesterday just for asking someone to move their tissue packet.

I want those tables freed up too, Wei Ling, but 60% of our morning customers come alone and carry scalding hot trays of runny eggs and kopi. If we just ban saving seats with tissue packets, solo customers have nowhere to put their hot tray while queuing.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Booth lockup & staff safety: 4 booths (16 of 28 seats) are held for 2 hours on a single $2.20 drink ($420/morning lost), and 62-year-old Auntie Mary refuses to police seats after getting yelled at.
tradeOffs.question: How do we stop people from camping at the booths for hours without making Auntie Mary confront customers?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Solo diners with hot trays: 60% of morning customers dine solo carrying hot egg trays and kopi; a flat ban on saving tables leaves them stranded with hot food.
tradeOffs.question: How does a solo customer with a hot tray get a guaranteed spot to sit?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Booth wall plugs & Wi-Fi: The 12 booth sockets and guest Wi-Fi run on a smart switch in the back room, so how we manage power and table layout determines whether people camp.
tradeOffs.question: What should we do with the booth power sockets, Wi-Fi, or table layout during the morning rush?

agenda.title: SFA food safety inspection & salmonella report
agenda.decision: how do we handle tomorrow's SFA inspection and salmonella report without sparking a media panic or wiping out 60% of our breakfast sets?

openingViews.view: A customer from yesterday's trial was hospitalized with suspected salmonella, and Straits Times reporters arrive tomorrow at 8am right before food safety inspectors come at 9am. Even though hospital lab results take 48 hours, I think we should stop serving soft-boiled eggs tomorrow morning so the press sees us being careful.

Stopping soft-boiled eggs wipes out 60% of our breakfast sets—about $1,800 tomorrow morning—and our egg warmer actually dipped to 58 degrees for 45 minutes during yesterday's rush instead of staying at 63 degrees. We have two unopened cartons of safe, pasteurized backup eggs in the storeroom that we can run at 63 degrees if we clean the tank tonight.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 8am press arrival: Straits Times journalists arrive at 8am while the hospital lab test takes 48 hours; we need a clear, honest answer for reporters without causing a panic.
tradeOffs.question: What do we tell the 8am reporters and customers while the hospital lab test is still pending?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Egg warmer temperature dip: Our egg water bath dipped to 58°C yesterday (needs 63°C), and inspectors will swab it at 9am, though we have two unopened cartons of pasteurized backup eggs.
tradeOffs.question: Do we take soft-boiled eggs off the menu tomorrow, or clean the water bath and use our pasteurized backup eggs at 63°C?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 9am inspection & $1,800 breakfast sales: Soft-boiled eggs are in 60% of breakfast sets ($1,800/morning), and inspectors at 9am will check our temperature logbook.
tradeOffs.question: How do we make sure the kitchen passes the 9am inspection check without losing our morning breakfast sales?

agenda.title: Delivery platform 32% commission squeeze
agenda.decision: how do we protect breakfast margins against 32% delivery commissions without losing 50% of our CBD corporate morning volume?

openingViews.view: GrabFood and Foodpanda just raised their delivery fee to 32%, which means we lose 40 cents on every $10 breakfast set we deliver. The problem is that half of our morning sales—about $2,400 every morning—come from nearby office towers ordering on those apps, and if we pull off the apps, those offices will order from Ya Kun instead.

And we can't simply mark up our $10 set to $13 on GrabFood, Daniel, because the app penalizes shops that charge higher prices online than in-store by hiding them in search results. Plus, our own website QR code only lets customers order for self-pickup since we don't have delivery riders.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 32% app fee vs $2,400 office sales: Delivery apps take 32% (losing $0.40 on every $10 single set), but leaving the apps hands $2,400 every morning in nearby office orders to Ya Kun.
tradeOffs.question: How do we stop losing money on single $10 delivery sets without losing our nearby office customers?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: App price rules & no delivery riders: Raising single-set prices on GrabFood gets our shop hidden in search results (though multi-set office platters count as a separate menu item), and our own QR link only does self-pickup.
tradeOffs.question: How should we set up our GrabFood menu or our self-pickup QR option so we don't get penalized by the app?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Counter staffing during rush: We cannot pull our counter staff off the line to hand-deliver orders to office towers during the 8am rush.
tradeOffs.question: How do we fulfill these office orders tomorrow morning without pulling our shop staff off the counter?

situation: We reopen our refurbished Nanyang Kopi & Toast flagship at Raffles Place tomorrow at 8:00 AM.

glossary.Kopi O Kosong: black coffee with no sugar and no milk
glossary.Teh C Siew Dai: hot tea with evaporated milk and less sugar
glossary.chope: reserving a kopitiam table by leaving a packet of tissue paper or lanyard on it
glossary.Set A: kaya butter toast with two soft-boiled eggs and a hot kopi or tea
glossary.POS: point-of-sale system (the self-order kiosk, cashier screen, and kitchen docket printer)
glossary.SFA: Singapore Food Agency (the national food hygiene and safety regulator)
glossary.Auntie Mary: our 62-year-old floor staff member who clears trays and wipes tables
glossary.kiosk: the 15-inch self-order touchscreens at the front of the outlet
